solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One being strung along by an unseen hand?

definitions.text: One being strung along by an unseen hand?

parts.words: One being strung along by an unseen hand?
parts.note: reads like someone being deceived by a hidden manipulator, but literally describes a puppet on strings worked from above

explanation.surface: Someone is being fooled by a hidden schemer pulling the strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strung along' usually means deceived; here it is literal: a puppet hangs on strings worked by a puppeteer out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings from a hidden operator is exactly this kind of figure.

clue.text: Those leading men order advance towards one surrounding castle

indicators.note: the leading letters of the next four words are taken, the ones at the front of each

explanation.surface: Commanders tell their troops to push forward against a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those leading' takes the first letters of men, order, advance and towards.
explanation.definitionFit: A water-filled ditch was dug around a castle as a defence.

clue.text: Harsh-sounding quality of choppy body of water

parts.note: choppy water is rough
Loch Ness is a famous Scottish body of water

explanation.surface: Describes the grating noise made by a rough lake or sea.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is borrowed from Loch Ness, the Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating or rasping tone in a voice or sound is described as its roughness.

clue.text: Beastly type of cad bumping off leading Republican

indicators.note: to bump off is to kill, so the named letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a cad is a rotter, an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel

indicators.note: the leading letter of Republican, its first

explanation.surface: A villainous scoundrel murders a top Republican politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests nasty, but it means animal: the definition is a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a 'beastly type' in the literal sense: a type of beast, a river mammal.

clue.text: Account for old idea I entertained

parts.note: ex means former, old, as in ex-husband

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so the letter goes inside the word for idea

parts.note: a plan is an idea or scheme

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to justify an outdated notion they once held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertained' means having a guest in, so the letter I sits within the word for idea; 'old' is the familiar prefix for former.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account of something is to make it clear, to give reasons for it.

clue.text: Almost irrelevant chap who's always in The Sun?

definitions.meaning: the word as an adjective means touching at one point only, so barely connected

definitions.text: chap who's always in The Sun?
definitions.meaning: a gentleman who is always in the sunshine would be tanned

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist always in The Sun tabloid is dismissed as nearly pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but the second definition wants the sunshine: a man always in it is a tan gent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangent or tangential only touches the subject, so it is barely relevant.

clue.text: Large drink or single

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
'one' is a drink, as in 'a quick one' at the pub

explanation.surface: A bar order: one big drink, or a single measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' for a drink is informal, as in 'fancy one?' for a drink at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Lone and single both mean solitary, being just one by itself.

clue.text: Old king wearing red and orangey-yellow

indicators.note: the king wears the red, so the word for red goes round the king's letter

parts.note: Che Guevara was a revolutionary, a red
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch dressed in red and yellowy-orange robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' is a communist, CHE (Guevara), not a colour; 'wearing' puts R inside CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment ranging from pale yellow to orange-brown.

clue.text: Going around north, peer tries careers in undertaking

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for north, enclosing it
to career is to rush wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A nobleman, heading north, tries out a series of jobs as a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' is a verb (to rush wildly), the anagram signal, not jobs; 'Going around' wraps the scrambled letters about the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a project or venture, something undertaken.

clue.text: Perhaps release English teacher one charged

parts.note: Miss is how pupils address a female teacher
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: An English teacher who was charged might be let go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a criminal charge; it is electric charge, giving ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is a giving off of gas, heat or light, an example of a release.

clue.text: One too old to be one of the boys in blue

definitions.text: One too old to be one of the boys in blue

parts.words: One too old to be one of the boys in blue
parts.note: seems to be about a retired police officer, but means a grown-up, past being a boy, with 'blue' hinting at films for grown-ups

explanation.surface: Someone has aged out of the police, the boys in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boys in blue' suggests police; the clue simply means a grown-up, no longer a boy, and blue (risqué) content is labelled for grown-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown man is too old to count as one of the boys.

clue.text: Criticise a mother that initially polished off nut topping?

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: polished off means finished or removed, and 'initially' says it is the first letter of the word that goes

explanation.surface: A cook slates their mother for wolfing down the nut garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' is slang for the head, not food; 'initially polished off' removes T from THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for head, and this straw hat from Ecuador sits on top of it.

clue.text: Want strong drink with mangoes on occasion

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a strong drink

indicators.note: only some of the letters, every other one, appear, as things done on occasion are done now and then

explanation.surface: Someone craves a stiff drink served with mango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb (desire); it is a noun meaning lack. 'On occasion' takes alternate letters A, G, E from mangoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or need means a scarcity of something.

clue.text: Box containing equestrian leader's lance

indicators.note: the word for box holds the next letter within it

parts.note: to spar is to box

indicators.note: the leader of equestrian is its first letter

explanation.surface: A storage box holds the lance belonging to the head rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' is the verb, to fight, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long pointed weapon, a kind of spear.

clue.text: Senior MP so in trouble for a slip of the tongue

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in a mess, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior politician in hot water after a verbal gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' rearranges SENIOR MP SO.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of verbal slip swaps the opening sounds of words, named after Rev. William Spooner.

clue.text: Break into piano performing in English city

indicators.note: the break is put into the other letters

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
on means performing, as an actor on stage
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Taking a break at the piano while performing in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break into' reads like burgling a piano; REST goes into P and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Preston is a city in Lancashire, northwest England.

clue.text: One switching sides to see one performing on film

parts.note: a turn is a performer, especially an act on a variety bill
a coat is a thin layer, like a film of paint

explanation.surface: Someone goes to the cinema to watch an actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' is a thin layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitor who changes allegiance is said to have turned their coat.

clue.text: I make use of loaf and trifle with hot filling

indicators.note: the letter for hot fills the word for trifle, going inside it

parts.note: to tinker is to trifle or fiddle with something
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A baker uses bread and a trifle dessert with a warm filling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' is slang for head (use your loaf), not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who thinks uses their head, and loaf is rhyming slang for head (loaf of bread).

clue.text: Practical skill shown by legend cooking with wok

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being worked on, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A famous chef shows off their skills stir-frying in a wok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' rearranges LEGEND and WOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Know-how gained from experience is practical expertise.

clue.text: Watch old boy start court action, perhaps

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
in tennis, a serve starts the action on court

explanation.surface: A former pupil watches a lawsuit get under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' suggests a lawsuit; it is tennis, where the serve starts play.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to watch it closely.

clue.text: Country City and United really love (not European)

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

indicators.note: not says leave out, and the letter for European is E

parts.note: to adore is to love greatly

explanation.surface: A football fan adores both Manchester City and United, but is not European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is the City of London, postcode EC; 'not European' drops an E from ADORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecuador is a South American country on the equator.

clue.text: Tory party primarily repels socialist high- flyers

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
a do is a party

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of repels

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for socialist

explanation.surface: A Conservative gathering mainly fends off left-wing high achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flyers' suggests ambitious people; it is literal: big birds that soar.
explanation.definitionFit: Condors are huge vultures of the Americas that soar at great heights.

clue.text: Guy hosting nude floor show

indicators.note: the word for guy hosts the other, holding it inside

parts.note: cat is slang for a man, a guy
bare means naked, nude

explanation.surface: A man throws a naked party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosting' means the slang word for a man holds the word for naked inside it; cat as 'guy' is jazz-era slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is entertainment performed in a nightclub or restaurant, often on the floor among tables.

clue.text: Set of moral principles used in Nazareth I corrupted

indicators.note: the answer is used within the next words, its letters run across them

explanation.surface: Values found in Nazareth were said to have been corrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used in' points into NazarETH I Corrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral code, a body of principles guiding conduct.

clue.text: Animal desire in husband on foremost of aphrodisiacs

indicators.note: the desire goes in, between the other letters
in a down clue, one piece is placed on top of the next
foremost means first, so the opening letter of aphrodisiacs

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A husband's lust is driven chiefly by aphrodisiacs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' stacks H above A; 'in' sets YEN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is an African and Asian carnivore known for its laughing call.

clue.text: What one could put up to protect against cats and dogs?

definitions.text: What one could put up to protect against cats and dogs?

parts.words: What one could put up to protect against cats and dogs?
parts.note: sounds like a fence against pets, but 'raining cats and dogs' means heavy rain

explanation.surface: Asks what barrier would keep cats and dogs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's raining cats and dogs' is an idiom for pouring rain, and 'put up' is what you do to open this.
explanation.definitionFit: You open this shelter over your head to keep off heavy rain.

clue.text: Issues the enemy raised somewhere at the front

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: time is called the enemy, as in 'how goes the enemy?'

indicators.note: the letter at the front of somewhere, its first

explanation.surface: Newspaper issues about the foe being reared up at the battlefront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The enemy' is a stock phrase for time; 'raised' turns TIME to EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something is to send it out, to give off or discharge it.

clue.text: Male on dope in church service

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A man high on drugs turns up in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' tempts as drugs; it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass is the Roman Catholic Eucharist service.

clue.text: Awful acne riled a person from another country

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Bad spots have upset a visiting foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges ACNE RILED.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iceland is from a nation other than one's own.

clue.text: Country of origin of Isaac Newton, the King's former wife and BA ultimately

indicators.note: the origin of each name is its first letter

parts.note: Diana was the first wife of King Charles III

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of BA

explanation.surface: Asks where Newton, the King's ex and British Airways all came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country of origin' is a red herring: 'Country' is the definition, 'origin of' gives the initials IN.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large country of South Asia.

clue.text: Dinner for one

parts.note: suggests a solitary supper, but means dinner is one example of this

explanation.surface: A table set for a single diner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Dinner, for one' as 'dinner, for example': it is one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is an instance of the general term for an occasion of eating.

clue.text: Those demonstrating toy with store reps around Sept. 4th

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the chosen letter
to toy with something is to play with it, so these letters are shuffled
the fourth letter of the abbreviation is picked out

explanation.surface: Sales reps fiddle with stock around early September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toy with' shuffles the two words, and 'around' wraps them about the fourth letter of the month abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters hold demonstrations against something.
